chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Ayoub from Abu Ubaydah who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Narrate to me what I can benefit with.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Ubaydah! Frequently remember death, for a person does not frequently mention it except that he becomes ascetic in the world.'

key_terms.زَهِدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا: Became ascetic in the world / Detached from worldly life

ai.seo_question: How does remembering death help in achieving spiritual detachment from the world?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the frequent remembrance of death (dhikr al-mawt) as the primary spiritual remedy for cultivating zuhd (asceticism). This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on mortality not as a source of despair, but as a transformative tool that naturally diminishes attachment to the transient world, aligning the believer’s heart with eternal values.
